findings.description: `changesOnlyUntested` still runs an unanchored `ls-tree`, so the case-fold check can be emptied and the test stage skipped.
findings.body:
**`changesOnlyUntested` still runs a listing that is not anchored at the root.** A session can use it to empty the case-fold check and skip the test stage.

ADR 0161 says that, for a key a live session sets after the last check, "each listing a stage reads is anchored at the root". This PR added `--full-tree` to `readBranchTree` (L410), and `targetHolds` already has it. The listing a few lines below, in the same function, was missed:

```ts
for (const path of runGit(repoPath, ['ls-tree', '-r', '-z', '--name-only', branch]).split('\0')) {
```

https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/6f0d161f823aab76bfb38ecacc60fd8fb645a22f/src/core/merge-gate.service.ts#L2448-L2458

This listing builds the case-fold `spellings` map. It runs in the main checkout (`req.repoPath`, called at L2627, after the build stage). Nothing pins the work tree for it, so a `core.worktree` aimed at the checkout's parent runs it from a subdirectory. The new suite shows what happens then: `merge-gate-shared-config.test.ts` asserts that `ls-tree -r --name-only pup/s1` returns `''` once the key is set.

**Trigger:**
1. The branch changes only paths on `UNTESTED_PATH_GLOBS`, such as `docs/x.md`. The tree also holds `docs/x.MD`, which a test reads (decision 78/139).
2. After `cutGateCheckout`'s check, while the build stage runs, a live session sets `core.worktree` to the checkout's parent.
3. `spellings` comes back empty, so `foldsOntoAnother` is false for every path. `rawDiffEntries` and `readBranchTree` are anchored, so nothing else in the function fails.
4. `untested` is true, `test` is `undefined` (L2640), and the hard test stage reports "no testable file changed".
5. The session clears the key before the post-stage `assertNoSharedWorktreeKey`. In `regateMerged` (`src/core/regate.service.ts` ~L200-220) the session does not even need to clear it, because that path has no post-stage check.

The ADR has the same gap. Its "anchored" list and its open-gap list (`docs/adr/0161-…md` L33-54) both leave this call out, so a reader would think every gate listing is covered. Either anchor the call, or name it in the ADR.

Three reviewers (correctness ×2, security) raised this separately, and the docs reviewer raised the ADR side.

findings.description: `diffHunks` swapped `--literal-pathspecs` for `:(top,literal)<path>`; an inherited `GIT_LITERAL_PATHSPECS=1`, which `scrubbedGitEnv` keeps, makes git read the whole string as a literal file name, so every file has no hunks and patch coverage passes.
findings.body:
**An inherited `GIT_LITERAL_PATHSPECS` now switches off the new pathspec magic, and coverage passes without checking anything.**

Before this PR, `diffHunks` passed `--literal-pathspecs` and a plain path. It now passes `` `:(top,literal)${path}` `` and drops the flag:

https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/6f0d161f823aab76bfb38ecacc60fd8fb645a22f/src/core/git-diff.client.ts#L661-L671

When `GIT_LITERAL_PATHSPECS` is set, git treats every pathspec literally and parses no magic. In `pathspec.c`, `parse_element_magic` returns the element as it is when `get_literal_global()` is true. `scrubbedGitEnv` starts from all of `process.env` and removes only `GIT_DIR`, `GIT_WORK_TREE`, `GIT_INDEX_FILE`, `GIT_COMMON_DIR`, `GIT_PREFIX` and the `GIT_CONFIG_*` keys (https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/6f0d161f823aab76bfb38ecacc60fd8fb645a22f/src/core/git-diff.client.ts#L29-L36). `GIT_HISTORY_ENV` does not override the variable either.

**How the variable gets set.** `git --literal-pathspecs` exports it to every child, and Magit runs git that way. A git alias or hook that runs `pup` from there passes it on, and an operator can also export it. Before this PR the variable did the same as the argv flag already passed, so it changed nothing.

**What breaks.** Git looks for a file literally named `:(top,literal)src/a.ts`, so every `diffHunks` call returns `[]`:
- `gitDiffAddedLines` returns `{}`, so patch coverage finds nothing to check and passes.
- `gitDiffBinaryRecount` returns `{0, 0}`, so a text file a `-diff` attribute forged into `-\t-` counts as zero lines (decision 53).

The new `':(top)'` in `filesNaming` (merge-gate.service.ts L555) has the same problem: grep looks for a file named `:(top)`, finds no importer, and the stage treats that as "nothing matched". `GIT_ICASE_PATHSPECS` used to fail loudly against `--literal-pathspecs`, but now it quietly adds `icase`.

**Fix.** Remove the four global pathspec variables in `scrubbedGitEnv` (`GIT_LITERAL_PATHSPECS`, `GIT_GLOB_PATHSPECS`, `GIT_NOGLOB_PATHSPECS`, `GIT_ICASE_PATHSPECS`), so every pathspec pup passes is parsed as written. This claim rests on git's pathspec internals and was not run under CI, so confidence is medium.

findings.description: The re-gate path never does the post-stage `core.worktree` check. `gateAndMerge` re-asks `assertNoSharedWorktreeKey` and `assertNoWorktreeConfig` after its last stage (merge-gate.service.ts L2061-2064, L2086-2091). The ADR says that check exists so "a key a session set while the stages ran is refused, not merged". `regateMerged` runs the same stages through `measureBranch`, but its only check is in `cutGateCheckout`. It then goes straight to `rewritePullRequest` and `assertPullRequestHead`, which publish a pass on the PR, with no further check.
ADR 0161 says "The ADR-number stage (decision 146) anchors its own reads", but no `docs/adr/0146*` exists and no ADR-number stage is in `src/`, so a reader can't verify the claim or find that stage.

The test is still titled "refuses a driver set in the session worktree's own config", and its old comment still explains the driver check. It now asserts `WorktreeConfigError`, thrown before the driver check runs, so the title and comment describe a path the test no longer reaches. Retitle it, or merge the old and new comments.

The pair `assertNoSharedWorktreeKey(repo); assertNoWorktreeConfig(repo);` now appears at four sites, past AGENTS.md's "third use" bar. One private helper in merge-gate.service.ts would hold both calls and their order (key first, because an empty key stops every git), and each site would keep its own WHY comment.

No guard test enforces ADR 0161's rule that every gate listing is anchored at the root (`--no-relative`, `--full-tree`, `:(top)`). A future gate `ls-tree`, `grep` or `diff` without those flags would silently list one subdirectory, and the case-fold `ls-tree` in `changesOnlyUntested` already slipped through this way. Only the per-site behavioural tests catch it.

The new `rawDiffEntries` sentence ("`--no-relative`, so a shared-config `core.worktree` running git from a subdirectory cannot narrow the listing...") repeats the `DIFF_SAFE_FLAGS` JSDoc in `git-diff.client.ts`. Replace it with a pointer such as "`--no-relative`: see `DIFF_SAFE_FLAGS`", or drop it.

The final-site comment says "Both go first: an empty key stops every git." That fact is already in the `assertNoSharedWorktreeKey` JSDoc ("empty, it stops every git in the repo"). The part about `fastForward` pinning `--work-tree` is specific to this site and worth keeping; only the empty-key clause is a duplicate.

The PR description promises things the diff doesn't contain: ADR-number lookalikes under Unicode case folding, pinning `core.worktree=` in GIT_SAFE_CONFIG (ADR 0161 explains why that is impossible), and `GIT_GRAFT_FILE=/dev/null` (the existing pin is `/dev/null/no-grafts`). Update the body so it matches what ships.

process_issues.description: The consolidator put three importants in one group (correctness ×2 and security, all on the unanchored ls-tree at merge-gate.service.ts:2453). I sent the clearest of the three (correctness, high) to validation as the representative, not all three. A separate docs important (the ADR leaves out the same listing) was validated on its own and confirmed. Since all of them describe one confirmed root cause, I folded them into a single posted important after validation; merged_duplicates=3.

Skipped areas: context (no spec, protocol or infra surface touched), workflow-safety (no .github/workflows change), spec (no closing issue or --spec source; the PR body is the only intent), and maintainability (not on the default roster).
